Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain. [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Focal osteochondral injury at the medial tibial plateau near the medial joint line with adjacent confluent bone marrow edema. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. Small leaking Baker's cyst with internal calcific body. Multiple intra-articular bodies, including a 1.1 cm ossific body at the anterior joint recess and a 0.8 cm ossific body at the posterior joint recess. Post arthroscopy scarring of Hoffa's fat pad.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tear of the medial meniscus, with maceration and complete radial tear at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. Posterior medial displacement of a meniscal flap in the region of the posterior root. Severe meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity with confluent regions of full-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity with areas of high-grade fissuring at the weightbearing aspect of the joint.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Confluent full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the lateral patellar facet and lateral trochlea. Articular surface remodeling at the lateral patellar facet. High-grade articular cartilage loss at the medial trochlea and medial facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Scarring.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon. Fragmentation of the tibial tubercle, reflecting the chronic sequela of remote Osgood-Schlatter disease.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Small subchondral insufficiency fracture at the medial tibial plateau near the medial joint line with associated confluent bone marrow edema. No significant articular surface depression.
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartments, where it is severe. Small knee joint effusion with multiple ossific intra-articular bodies measuring up to 1.1 cm. Small leaking Baker's cyst.
3.	Complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus with dominant radial tear at the posterior horn-posterior root junction. Displacement of a meniscal flap to the posteromedial joint recess.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Mild degenerative subchondral cystic changes are present at the anterior weightbearing aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and at the anterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Mild, diffuse synovial proliferation. Moderate size Baker cyst. Small ganglion cyst also arises from the gastrocnemius origins bilaterally.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear involving the posterior horn extending to the meniscal body. Mild extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is moderate cartilage thinning and irregularity diffusely. Small marginal osteophytes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is a large, complex tear involving the anterior horn, body and posterior horn, with maceration and moderate extrusion. A prominent radial tear is present at the junction of the body and posterior horn. A fragment is displaced centrally toward the intercondylar notch.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is marked, diffuse cartilage loss with large marginal osteophytes.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is moderate cartilage thinning and surface irregularity at the patella and trochlea diffusely. Moderate osteophytes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): The anterior cruciate ligament is diffusely degenerated. Both bundles are not well visualized, suggesting chronic partial tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Degenerated, intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
There is mild anterior soft tissue edema. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Medial and lateral meniscal tear. Maceration and extrusion of the lateral meniscus.
2. Tricompartmental osteoarthritis most prominent in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment.
3. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament with evidence of chronic partial tear.
4. Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation. Moderate Baker cyst.

Interprétation: 

Dans l’intervalle, il y a eu progression d’un épanchement intra-articulaire d’allure modérée à large avec signes de synovite chronique. Il y a également augmentation en taille d’un kyste de Baker multi-lobulé, non-compliqué s’étendant sur 4.4cm de diamètre CC. 

Il y a une déchirure légèrement complexe du ménisque interne dans l’intervalle avec une composante probablement longitudinale oblique à la jonction de la corne postérieure et du corps méniscal avec flap méniscal déplacé au sein de la gouttière antérosupérieure à l’interligne articulaire fémoro-tibial interne. Il y a extrusion modérée du ménisque résiduel. 

Il y a progression d’une chondropathie maintenant sévère (grade 4) au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne avec dénudation transfixiante des surfaces cartilagineuses et changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ostéophytes marginaux modérés. 

Le ligament collatéral interne est intact sans déchirure. 

Léger émoussement du rebord libre de la corne postérieur du ménisque externe sans déchirure méniscale significative. Atténuation chondrale légère à modérée au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe avec fissures chondrales partielles en lien avec une chondropathie de grade 2. Il n’y a pas d’évidence d’atteinte transfixiante ou changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ostéophytose modérée. Le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe est intact sans déchirure. Il y a multiples kystes ganglionnaires en lien avec la jonction myotendineuse et le récessus poplité au versant postéro-externe du genou. 

Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. 

L’alignement fémoro-patellaire demeure dans les limites normales. Les tendons du quadriceps distal et patellaire sont intacts sans déchirure. Il y a une atténuation diffuse modérée des surfaces chondrales, avec foyer de chondropathie de grade 4 similaire le long de la facette patellaire interne avec fissure transfixiante et début de changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés et de grade 3 au niveau de l’échancrure inter-condylienne avec fissure chondrale transfixiante. Petits ostéophytes marginaux. 

Œdème sous-cutané pré-patellaire et infra-patellaire, non-spécifique. 

Conclusion: 

Il y a une nouvelle déchirure légèrement complexe dans l’intervalle impliquant le ménisque interne avec composante longitudinale oblique à la jonction de la corne postérieure et du corps méniscal et flap méniscal déplacé au sein de la gouttière antéro-supérieure à l’interligne articulaire fémoro-tibial interne tel que décrit ci-haut. 

Il y a progression d’une chondropathie fémoro-tibiale principalement interne, avec atteinte de grade 4. 

Progression d’un épanchement intra-articulaire maintenant modéré à large et d’un kyste de Baker non-compliqué avec signes de synovite associés. 

Il n’y a pas d’autre changement significatif dans l’intervalle incluant une chondropathie de grade 4 le long de la facette patellaire interne.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Clicking, locking, exclude meniscal tear..

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination. The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta. The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.6.
The finding is associated with advanced patellofemoral joint osteoarthritic change with extensive denuding of the articular cartilage and with extensive subcortical cyst formation particularly seen along the apex and lateral facet of patella. Prominent trochlear and patellar osteophytes are demonstrated.

The medial patellar retinaculum is attenuated likely related to previous lateral dislocation and partial disruption. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

There is a degenerative medial meniscal tear. There is maceration and linear signal seen in the posterior horn extending into the body. An oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the body and posterior horn is a demonstrated. The finding is associated with severe chondral denuding and exuberant marginal osteophyte formation seen to the medial joint compartment. There is also subcortical edema seen to the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

The lateral meniscus is macerated and not identified at the body and posterior horn. Findings are in keeping with extensive maceration and degenerative tearing of the body and the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. The finding is associated with denuding of the entire articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment associated with prominent lateral joint compartment osteophyte formation. There is also subcortical sclerosis and mild edema seen within the lateral joint compartment. An intraosseous cyst is seen to the lateral femoral condyle with 3 cm in keeping with subcortical tear.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligament are intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is a large knee effusion with reactive synovitis. There is no significant Baker's cyst. In the lateral popliteal fossa there is a large intraosseous loose body projecting anterior to the proximal fibers of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius measuring about 2.4 cm in maximum dimension. Smaller loose bodies are likely present in this region.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritic change most severely affecting patellofemoral and lateral compartments. Degenerative meniscal tears laterally and medially with cartilaginous denuding to the lateral medial and patellofemoral compartments.

Loose bodies.

Patella alta with attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum likely related to prior transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain in right knee, primary osteoarthritis.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Subchondral insufficiency fracture central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle as well as the adjacent tibia with moderate bone marrow edema. No articular surface collapse or osteonecrosis. 
Subcortical cyst identified in the head of the fibula. Mild to moderate osteophyte formation within all 3 compartments of the knee.
Background bone marrow signal is normal. No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate, partially ruptured Baker cyst. Moderate joint effusion. Diffuse synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Large, complex tear of the body and posterior horn. There is marked extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Severe, diffuse cartilage loss. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT: 
Lateral meniscus: Small tear at posterior root.  
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage thinning and fissuring at the weightbearing aspect. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patella cartilage: Moderate to severe cartilage loss, lateral greater than medial.
Femoral trochlea cartilage: Mild to moderate cartilage thinning diffusely. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal. 
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate tendinosis without tear.
Patella tendon: Mild tendinosis without tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: There is a mild amount of edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation.  No patella alta.  Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. 

SOFT TISSUES:
Varicose veins identified in the medial subcutaneous fat. 
Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Compared to the prior exam, medial meniscal tear and chondrosis in the medial tibiofemoral compartment have progressed. Subchondral insufficiency fractures at the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau are new.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Subchondral insufficiency fractures at the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.
2. Large, complex tear of the medial meniscus with marked extrusion. Small tear at the posterior root attachment of the lateral meniscus.
3. Tricompartmental chondrosis, most prominent in the medial tibiofemoral compartment.
4. Quadriceps and patellar tendinosis.
5. Moderate, ruptured Baker cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE]  [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 7 months. No known injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Acute subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle. Confluent subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. Normal background marrow signal. Proximal patellar enthesophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus. Superiorly displaced meniscal flap at the medial joint line and at the posterior horn. Severe meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large confluent regions of full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint. High-grade cartilage loss at the posterior medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small complex tear of the lateral meniscal body, characterized by a dominant horizontal component.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity at the weightbearing aspect of the joint without focal defect.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness chondral defect at the lateral patellar facet measuring 6 x 6 mm. Focal full-thickness fissuring at the patellar median ridge. Areas of full-thickness fissuring at the medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Chronic partial tearing at the femoral attachment of the fibular collateral ligament.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 15 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Intramuscular edema at the popliteus and tibialis anterior, possibly reflecting low-grade strains. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. Deep soft tissue edema at the posterior thigh. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the weightbearing medial femoral condyle without articular surface collapse. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. 
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion with synovitis.
3.	Complex degenerative tearing throughout the medial meniscus with multiple displaced meniscal flaps and severe meniscal extrusion.
4.	Complex tearing of the lateral meniscal body.
5.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, severe in the medial compartment.
